newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-MIM says Ernest Henry will proceed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-MIM says Ernest Henry will proceed.

text.p: MIM Holdings Ltd said on Friday that the development of the Ernest Henry copper-gold joint venture project will continue despite potential native title claims that threaten to halt the project.
"Ernest Henry Mining Pty Ltd will continue to develop the mine and it will come into production later next year," MIM's public affairs manager, Collin Myers told Reuters.
"Any native title claim will not affect EHM's right to mine the project," Myers said.

The Ernest Henry mine, near Cloncurry in western Queensland, has been threatened with a native title claim by local Aboriginal groups as well as a separate application for an injunction to halt a power link to the mine site.
A decision on the injunction application is due to be handed down in the Brisbane Federal Court on Friday morning.

MIM said on Thursday the native title claim sought compensation of A$120 million but aboriginal consultant and negotiator Charles Perkins told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio that a set amount had not been officially mentioned.
"We'll be monitoring the situation closely," Myers said.
MIM said that Sancave Pty Ltd, a company associated with local Aboriginal interests, was seeking A$120 million to ensure no native title claim was made on the mine or its power or water supply.
MIM, as 51 percent owner and operator and its 49 percent partner Savage Resources Ltd said they rejected the proposal as "not an acceptable basis for negotiations".

In a separate application on Monday, the Kalkadoon Dancers' Association applied to the Federal Court for an injunction to prevent the North Queensland Electricity Commission from continuing work on the mine's power link between Mt Isa and Ernest Henry.
The Ernest Henry mine is due for start up late in 1997 and is expected to be producing at an annual rate of 95,000 tonnes of copper and 120,000 ounces of gold.
